## ff4dfc92ad29

**Reproduced semantic shortcut — bounding-box thickness is indistinguishable from onion depth on the generated domain.** Generator SHA-256 `dad618f6a14cbbcd22fa6d223fe37940e052438abf0b37d10d5a1a03be32f933` generates only solid rectangles and assigns each intended depth `d` a shorter side of `2d-1` or `2d`. Therefore the non-peeling rival “sort components by minimum bounding-box side, then color” has the same order as the intended onion-depth rule by construction.

I generated 64 lawful inputs—16 each for unspecified, easy, medium, and hard difficulty—and applied canonical Racket rule hash `75d947eae7f8` through the supported runner. The rival matched the Racket output on 64/64 generated inputs with no Racket errors, and it also matched all 3/3 canonical train/test pairs. All 64 generated inputs passed the target's `self_check`; the equivalence is inside the documented rectangle-only generator domain, not caused by malformed examples.

Evidence: `checks/audit/ff4dfc92ad29/counterexample.json`, `checks/audit/ff4dfc92ad29/input.json`, `checks/audit/ff4dfc92ad29/racket.json`, and `checks/audit/ff4dfc92ad29/rival_pre_apply.json`.

This does not prove the canonical task itself is uniquely identifiable from its three examples. It does show that this generator cannot teach onion peeling as distinct from a much simpler bounding-box heuristic. A future repair should include connected non-rectangular components whose onion depth is not monotone in minimum bounding-box side (and should declare/test that rival). No source was changed in this audit.

Findings-only report explicitly unresolved. Rectangle-only support makes bounding-box short-side sorting equivalent to onion depth:3 canonical slots and24 ordinary labels agree. Ring distinction is OUTSIDE validator/generated domain, not a sampled label error. Four of six exact9x14 requests silently widen; all31 actual Racket outputs valid. Existing same-source open teaching finding stays open. ## ff4dfc92ad29

**Reproduced teaching restriction and exact-override defect; findings only.** Audited generator SHA-256: `dad618f6a14cbbcd22fa6d223fe37940e052438abf0b37d10d5a1a03be32f933`. Executed rule hash: `75d947eae7f8`. No source for this audit target was changed.

The intended rule orders foreground objects by onion-peeling depth, with the rule's color tie break. The generator emits only solid rectangles. On those objects, ordering by the shorter bounding-box side is equivalent to ordering by depth. The bounding-box rival matches all three canonical labeled slots and all 24 ordinary generated inputs sampled across unspecified/easy/medium/hard difficulty. Every one of those 24 labels was obtained from fresh Racket execution and agreed with an independent onion implementation. This reproduces the same-source teaching restriction already noted in the source's open audit; it is not presented as a newly resolved finding.

A nonrectangular 7×7 color-7 ring, a solid 3×3 color-2 square and a solid 5×5 color-4 square give a concrete distinction: Racket returns `[[7,2,4]]`, whereas the bounding-box rival returns `[[2,4,7]]`. The exact 9×21 input is retained in `checks/audit/ff4dfc92ad29/inputs.json` and `confirmed.json`; input hash is `b0c3cff84e518a3bb46caf136ce1e2867d5dde4a88189c9d33b364d851f9483f`. The generator validator rejects the ring as nonrectangular. This is therefore a **rule-domain counterfactual outside generated/validator support**, not a claim of a mislabeled generated input. A maintainer decision is needed on whether broader shapes belong in the task domain; if so, the sampler and validator both need expansion.

Separately, exact requests `grid_h=9, grid_w=14`, easy difficulty, sample index 0, seeds 0–5 produce shapes 9×15, 9×14, 9×17, 9×18, 9×16 and 9×14. Four of six calls silently increase the requested width to fit the row packing. That is a concrete exact-control violation. Suggested repair: preserve the requested width and either construct a fitting instance or reject an infeasible override with an explicit error. The six override outputs also received fresh Racket labels; their semantic labels are correct despite the dimension contract defect.

Evidence: `checks/audit/ff4dfc92ad29/summary.json`, `probe.py`, `inputs.json`, `racket.json` and `confirmed.json`. Total actual Racket outputs checked: 31 (24 ordinary, six override cases and one ring counterfactual). The bounded sample does not certify the rest of the distribution.

triage.reason: Both exact-source peer reports explicitly unresolved; outside-domain ring witness, exact-width violation, and diagnostic query-rotation ambiguity retain distinct scopes. No audit-target edits or approval changes.
